tool_args.rationale: The five pilot rows span H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the H = 20 forecast. They support sink suppression but do not resolve whether slow adaptation eventually outweighs the fast positive response. The slow-horizon probe directly tests that distinction.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At short horizons, the slow adaptation term mainly constrains the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. A good pilot fit would not establish the sign or magnitude at H = 20.
It can explain gradient suppression but cannot predict a delayed reversal. The pilot does not distinguish it from the adaptation model at the forecast horizon.
Finer short-time sampling could resolve fast dynamics but would not directly test slow adaptation at the forecast horizon.
